# radosgw Provider

Terraform provider for managing Ceph RADOS Gateway (RadosGW) resources via Admin and S3 APIs.

## Required User Capabilities

The RadosGW user configured in this provider requires specific capabilities to manage different resources:

| Capability | Resources |
|------------|-----------|
| `accounts=*` | `radosgw_iam_account` (and the `account_id`/`account_root` attributes of `radosgw_iam_user`) |
| `users=*` |`radosgw_iam_user`, `radosgw_iam_subuser`, `radosgw_iam_access_key`, `radosgw_iam_user_caps`, `radosgw_iam_quota`, `radosgw_iam_user`, `radosgw_iam_users` |
| `buckets=*` | `radosgw_s3_bucket_link`; `radosgw_s3_bucket` (only for the Admin-API metadata — it falls back to the S3 API without this cap) |
| `ratelimit=*` | `radosgw_s3_bucket_rate_limit` |
| `oidc-provider=*` | `radosgw_iam_openid_connect_provider` |
| `roles=*` | `radosgw_iam_role`, `radosgw_iam_role_policy`, `radosgw_iam_roles` |
| `metadata=*` | `radosgw_iam_users` |

To grant all capabilities to a user:

```bash
radosgw-admin caps add --uid=admin --caps="accounts=*;buckets=*;metadata=*;oidc-provider=*;roles=*;users=*;ratelimit=*"
```

~> **These capabilities authorize the Admin Ops API and are cluster-wide** (not scoped to a tenant or account). The S3 bucket sub-resources (`radosgw_s3_bucket_acl`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_policy`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_notification`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_website_configuration`) and the IAM/STS resources (`radosgw_iam_role`, `radosgw_iam_role_policy`, `radosgw_iam_openid_connect_provider`, `radosgw_sns_topic`) use the S3/IAM APIs directly and need **no** admin capability — they work with the configured user's own S3/IAM permissions.

~> **Federated and account users.** A user authenticated via OpenStack Keystone, or an account root user, usually has no admin capabilities. Such users can still manage S3-based resources (for example `radosgw_s3_bucket` is created over the S3 API, with Admin-API-only metadata left `null`). Admin capabilities **can** be granted to an account user with `radosgw-admin caps add` to enable the Admin-API-backed resources — but this grants **cluster-wide** admin-ops access and is independent of the account's IAM policies (which govern that account's own S3/IAM data-plane actions).

~> **Managing users inside an account (least privilege).** A whole family of resources manages an account's IAM entities **through the account's IAM API** — so an **account root user** (or any account member holding the matching `iam:*` permission) can use them with **no admin capabilities at all**: `radosgw_iam_account_user`, `radosgw_iam_account_access_key`, `radosgw_iam_account_user_policy` (inline) / `radosgw_iam_account_user_policy_attachment` (managed), `radosgw_iam_account_group`, `radosgw_iam_account_group_membership`, `radosgw_iam_account_group_policy` / `radosgw_iam_account_group_policy_attachment`, plus the role resources `radosgw_iam_role`, `radosgw_iam_role_policy` (inline) / `radosgw_iam_role_policy_attachment` (managed) and `radosgw_iam_openid_connect_provider` (which also work in the non-account/tenant context). Configure the provider (typically an aliased instance) with the account root's credentials. Use these for least-privilege, per-account management; use `radosgw_iam_user` (which needs the cluster-wide `users` cap) when you need full RGW user metadata — display name, email, quotas, `op_mask`, suspension, caps, Swift subusers — or to create an account's **root** user.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Configure the RadosGW Provider
provider "radosgw" {
  # RadosGW endpoint URL (required)
  # Can also be set via RADOSGW_ENDPOINT environment variable
  endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:7480"

  # Access key for authentication
  # Required for static credentials and for assume_role; omit when using
  # assume_role_with_web_identity. Can also be set via RADOSGW_ACCESS_KEY.
  access_key = "admin-access-key"

  # Secret key for authentication
  # Required for static credentials and for assume_role; omit when using
  # assume_role_with_web_identity. Can also be set via RADOSGW_SECRET_KEY.
  secret_key = "admin-secret-key"
}

# Example using environment variables (recommended for production)
# export RADOSGW_ENDPOINT="http://rgw.example.com:7480"
# export RADOSGW_ACCESS_KEY="your-access-key"
# export RADOSGW_SECRET_KEY="your-secret-key"
#
# provider "radosgw" {}

# Example with TLS configuration using a CA certificate file
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint                  = "https://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key                = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key                = "admin-secret-key"
#   root_ca_certificate_file  = "/path/to/ca-cert.pem"
# }

# Example with TLS configuration using inline CA certificate
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint            = "https://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key          = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key          = "admin-secret-key"
#   root_ca_certificate = <<-EOT
#     -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
#     MIIDXTCCAkWgAwIBAgIJAJC1...
#     -----END CERTIFICATE-----
#   EOT
# }

# Example with insecure TLS (skip certificate verification for HTTPS)
# WARNING: Only use this for development or testing environments with self-signed certs
# Note: This option has no effect on plain HTTP connections
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint                   = "https://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key                 = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key                 = "admin-secret-key"
#   tls_insecure_skip_verify   = true
# }

# Assuming an IAM role (STS AssumeRole)
# The static access_key/secret_key are exchanged for temporary credentials for the
# role, which are then used for all S3 and IAM/STS calls. The role must already
# exist and its trust policy must allow these credentials to assume it.
# Note: the Admin Ops API cannot use the session token that comes with temporary
# credentials, so Admin-API-backed data is unavailable under an assumed role (the
# same behavior as a user without admin capabilities) — use it for S3 and IAM
# role/policy/OIDC resources.
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint   = "http://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key = "admin-secret-key"
#
#   assume_role {
#     # role_arn accepts the non-account form (arn:aws:iam:::role/<name>) or the
#     # account-scoped form (arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<name>).
#     role_arn     = "arn:aws:iam:::role/terraform"
#     session_name = "terraform"
#     # duration  = "1h"    # session lifetime (default 1h)
#     # Note: RadosGW does not support an external ID, so there is no external_id argument.
#   }
# }

# Assuming a role with an inline session policy (jsonencode)
# The session policy further restricts the assumed session. On RadosGW, use
# explicit Deny statements — allow-only scope-down (AWS implicit deny) is not
# enforced.
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint   = "http://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key = "admin-secret-key"
#
#   assume_role {
#     role_arn     = "arn:aws:iam:::role/terraform"
#     session_name = "terraform"
#
#     policy = jsonencode({
#       Version = "2012-10-17"
#       Statement = [
#         {
#           Sid      = "DenyBucketDeletion"
#           Effect   = "Deny"
#           Action   = ["s3:DeleteBucket"]
#           Resource = ["*"]
#         }
#       ]
#     })
#   }
# }

# Assuming a role with the session policy read from a file
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint   = "http://rgw.example.com:7480"
#   access_key = "admin-access-key"
#   secret_key = "admin-secret-key"
#
#   assume_role {
#     role_arn     = "arn:aws:iam:::role/terraform"
#     session_name = "terraform"
#     policy       = file("${path.module}/session-policy.json")
#   }
# }

# Assuming a role with a web identity token (OIDC federation)
# No static credentials are required — the OIDC JWT is the credential. The role's
# trust policy must federate the OIDC provider and permit the token's audience.
# Provide the token inline (web_identity_token) or from a file
# (web_identity_token_file) — exactly one of the two.
# provider "radosgw" {
#   endpoint = "http://rgw.example.com:7480"
#
#   assume_role_with_web_identity {
#     role_arn                = "arn:aws:iam:::role/terraform"
#     session_name            = "terraform"
#     web_identity_token_file = "/var/run/secrets/openid/token"
#     # web_identity_token    = var.oidc_token   # alternative to the file
#     # policy   = "..."   # optional inline session policy (JSON)
#     # duration = "1h"    # session lifetime (default 1h)
#   }
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `access_key` (String) RadosGW access key. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable. Required for static credentials and for `assume_role`; ignored (and not required) when `assume_role_with_web_identity` is used.
- `assume_role` (Block, Optional) Assume an IAM role (STS `AssumeRole`) using the configured `access_key`/`secret_key`, and use the resulting temporary credentials for all subsequent calls. The static credentials must be allowed to assume the role, and the role's trust policy must permit them. `role_arn` accepts both the non-account form (`arn:aws:iam:::role/<name>`) and the account-scoped form (`arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<name>`).

~> **Note:** Assumed-role (temporary) credentials carry a session token, which the S3 and IAM/STS APIs honor. The Admin Ops API cannot use a session token, so Admin-API-backed data (e.g. `num_shards`, `bucket_quota`, and the `radosgw_iam_user`/account-bootstrap resources) is unavailable under an assumed role — the same behavior as a user without admin capabilities. Use assumed-role credentials for S3 and IAM role/policy/OIDC resources.

~> **Note:** RadosGW does not support an external ID — a role whose trust policy includes an `sts:ExternalId` condition cannot be assumed — so there is no `external_id` argument. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assume_role))
- `assume_role_with_web_identity` (Block, Optional) Assume an IAM role with a web identity token (STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`), and use the resulting temporary credentials for all subsequent calls. The token is an OIDC JWT; this call is anonymous, so `access_key`/`secret_key` are **not** required. The role's trust policy must federate the OIDC provider and permit the token's audience. `role_arn` accepts both the non-account form (`arn:aws:iam:::role/<name>`) and the account-scoped form (`arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<name>`). Mutually exclusive with `assume_role`.

This block can also be configured entirely via environment variables — `RADOSGW_ROLE_ARN` (also activates web identity on its own), `RADOSGW_ROLE_SESSION_NAME`, `RADOSGW_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN`, and `RADOSGW_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` — with block values taking precedence over the environment.

~> **Note:** When web identity is used, static credentials (`access_key`/`secret_key` and `RADOSGW_ACCESS_KEY`/`RADOSGW_SECRET_KEY`) are ignored.

~> **Note:** As with `assume_role`, the resulting temporary credentials cannot drive the Admin Ops API (no session token support), so Admin-API-backed data is unavailable — use them for S3 and IAM role/policy/OIDC resources. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assume_role_with_web_identity))
- `endpoint` (String) RadosGW endpoint URL. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
- `root_ca_certificate` (String) PEM-encoded root CA certificate content to use for TLS verification. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROOT_CA_CERTIFICATE` environment variable.
- `root_ca_certificate_file` (String) Path to a PEM-encoded root CA certificate file to use for TLS verification. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROOT_CA_CERTIFICATE_FILE` environment variable.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) RadosGW secret key. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_SECRET_KEY` environment variable. Required for static credentials and for `assume_role`; ignored (and not required) when `assume_role_with_web_identity` is used.
- `tls_insecure_skip_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate verification for HTTPS connections. This is useful when connecting to RadosGW with self-signed certificates or certificates signed by an untrusted CA. Has no effect on plain HTTP connections. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` environment variable. Default is `false`.

<a id="nestedblock--assume_role"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assume_role`

Optional:

- `duration` (String) Lifetime of the assumed-role session, as a Go duration string (e.g. `1h`, `30m`). Defaults to `1h`. Subject to the role's maximum session duration.
- `policy` (String) An IAM policy document (JSON) applied as a session policy to further restrict the assumed-role session. **Note:** on RadosGW only explicit `Deny` statements are enforced — AWS-style scope-down via an allow-only policy (implicit deny of anything not listed) is **not** applied, so use explicit `Deny` statements to restrict a session.
- `role_arn` (String) ARN of the IAM role to assume, e.g. `arn:aws:iam:::role/my-role`.
- `session_name` (String) Session name to use when assuming the role. Defaults to `terraform`.


<a id="nestedblock--assume_role_with_web_identity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assume_role_with_web_identity`

Optional:

- `duration` (String) Lifetime of the assumed-role session, as a Go duration string (e.g. `1h`, `30m`). Defaults to `1h`. Subject to the role's maximum session duration.
- `policy` (String) An IAM policy document (JSON) applied as a session policy to further restrict the session. **Note:** on RadosGW only explicit `Deny` statements are enforced — allow-only scope-down is not applied.
- `role_arn` (String) ARN of the IAM role to assume, e.g. `arn:aws:iam:::role/my-role`. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROLE_ARN` environment variable.
- `session_name` (String) Session name to use when assuming the role. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROLE_SESSION_NAME` environment variable. Defaults to `terraform`.
- `web_identity_token` (String, Sensitive) The OIDC web identity token (JWT) to exchange for credentials. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN` environment variable. Exactly one web identity token source (`web_identity_token` or `web_identity_token_file`) must be set.
- `web_identity_token_file` (String) Path to a file containing the OIDC web identity token (JWT). Can be set via the `RADOSGW_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable. Exactly one web identity token source (`web_identity_token` or `web_identity_token_file`) must be set.
